title: Where to Eat on the Way to Erawan & Sai Yok 2026 | ThailandAddict
metaDesc: Restaurants and cafes to stop at on the drive to Erawan Falls (Route 3199) and Sai Yok (Route 323) in Kanchanaburi, Thailand — jungle-style giant catfish, riverside som tam and grilled chicken, cafes in the rice fields, with parking notes, rough prices, and opening hours.
keywords: restaurants on the way to Erawan, food stops Sai Yok, Kanchanaburi roadside cafes, Krua Khao Din, Amatala Coffee
h1:
Where to Eat on the Way
to Erawan & Sai Yok
intro: The drive from Kanchanaburi town out to Erawan Falls or Sai Yok takes a bit over an hour, and you can power through it in one go — but it's a lot more fun if you build in a few food stops along the way. The two routes split the moment you leave town: Route 3199 heads north toward Erawan and Si Sawat, while Route 323 runs west toward Sai Yok. We've picked places that are actually open and that locals and travelers mention often, lined up by stop so they're easy to fit into your drive.

blocks.html: Before you set off, getting the directions straight makes planning your stops much easier. Erawan Falls and Srinakarin Dam are out toward Si Sawat district, reached via Highway 3199 (the Lat Ya–Erawan road). Sai Yok and Sai Yok Noi Falls are a different way entirely, via Highway 323 heading toward the Three Pagodas Pass. Most of these places sit right along these two roads — easy to pull into, with parking, no need to wind down narrow side lanes.

This road is known for bold jungle-style cooking and restaurants along the Khwae Yai River. The closer you get to the dam, the more som tam and grilled-chicken spots with water views you'll find. If you're planning to swim at Erawan in the morning, eat your main meal on the way back in the afternoon — many of these places get packed at lunch on weekends.

items.name: Krua Khao Din
items.blurb: A bold jungle-style restaurant right on Route 3199 before you reach Erawan. Plenty of drivers heading up the Si Sawat road pull in here. Standout dishes are chu chee giant catfish, soft-bone tom yum, stir-fried fern with minced pork, and giant Mekong catfish fried with fish sauce. Reviewers agree the portions are generous and the flavors land.

items.name: Krua Rim Nam Nong Hoi
items.blurb: A fairly hidden jungle-style spot out near Ban Nong Hoi, close to Erawan, with a natural setting. The dishes people order most are spicy stir-fried wild boar, jungle curry with giant catfish, and termite mushrooms stir-fried in oyster sauce. Good for anyone who likes proper homestyle heat.
items.meta: Jungle-style Thai · short turn off the road

items.name: Phi Jo Tam Lan Khuean
items.blurb: A som tam and grilled-chicken place that's been going for decades, on the Khwae Yai side near Srinakarin Dam. The two-story building lets you sit and watch the water. Order som tam, grilled chicken, grilled pork neck, and mushroom soup — the standard local combo. Quick service.
items.meta: Isan / som tam · on the Khwae Yai

items.name: Som Tam Pak Ban
items.blurb: Som tam and grilled chicken on the Khwae Yai River, close to both Erawan Falls and Srinakarin Dam. Open, breezy setting by the water — a good, easy-on-the-wallet lunch stop before or after the falls.

items.name: Amatala Coffee Roaster
items.blurb: A coffee roastery and cafe about 5 km before Erawan, using beans from the hills around Si Sawat — roasted in-house, ground and brewed fresh. They have coffee, bakery, and food, plus seating with a natural view. A solid caffeine stop before you take on the falls.

items.name: Ban Ton Nam
items.blurb: A restaurant near Erawan National Park where travelers stop for lunch before or after hiking the falls. It's close to the park entrance, so it's an easy add-on — good if you don't want to drive around hunting for somewhere further off.
items.meta: Thai / made-to-order · near the falls entrance

blocks.title: Timing your stops right
blocks.html: If you want to swim at Erawan, aim to reach the park gate before 10 a.m. — it gets crowded and the parking fills up fast. Hit a cafe like Amatala in the morning for coffee, then save the heavy meal — jungle-style food or riverside som tam — for the afternoon on the way back, so you're not too full to climb the upper tiers of the falls.

Leaving town on Route 323, the first stretch passes through Wang Dong subdistrict, where there are cafes set in the rice fields with views toward Wat Tham Suea. Once you enter Sai Yok, it becomes local restaurants with bold flavors and spots along the Khwae Noi River. If you're heading to Sai Yok Noi Falls or doing a raft trip, these stops fall neatly along the way.

items.name: Meena Cafe
items.blurb: One of Kanchanaburi's original rice-field cafes, behind Wat Tham Suea in the Tha Muang–Wang Dong area. It's a popular photo stop before you get onto Route 323, with a wooden bridge over the paddies and hammock seating facing the view. Drinks run from a few tens of baht to around a hundred, and there are one-plate dishes too.

items.name: Ban Kafae
items.blurb: A roadside coffee shop on Route 323, on the way out of town toward Sai Yok, about 6 km from the center. An easy place to pull in for coffee as you start the drive — no need to turn off into a side lane.
items.price: Drinks from a few tens to ~THB 100

items.name: Krua Na Khwan
items.blurb: A bold, homestyle local restaurant Sai Yok–style, about 5 km before Sai Yok Noi Falls — just past the Sai Yok PTT station. A good lunch stop before you head into the falls.
items.meta: Homestyle local · near Sai Yok Noi

items.name: Renu Restaurant
items.blurb: A homestyle Thai restaurant in Sai Yok with a menu well over a hundred items. The dishes people order most are giant catfish fried with fish sauce, spicy stir-fried wild boar, and stir-fried local greens. Great if you're a group and want to order a spread to share.

items.name: Ban Tang Rim Khwae
items.blurb: A chilled-out spot on the Khwae Noi River around Sai Yok Yai, good for settling in and watching the water — more of a slow hangout than a quick bite. Pairs well with a raft trip or a stay at one of the floating raft houses nearby.

items.name: U Terrace River Kwai Cafe & Cuisine
items.blurb: A cafe-cum-restaurant on the river in Sai Yok, with both drinks and main dishes and a river view. A good place for a longer break on the way to or from the falls.

blocks.title: A few real things to know before you stop
blocks.html: Many riverside and jungle-style places are cash-mainly. Mobile signal is patchy in parts of Route 3199 and around Sai Yok, so carry cash and screenshot your map ahead of time. On weekends and long holidays the popular spots get long queues — if you're starving, a less-busy second choice will fill you up just as well.

blocks.text: How to pick stops that fit your trip

items: Out in the morning, back in the afternoon (Erawan) — coffee at Amatala on the way up, swim at the falls, then jungle-style food or riverside som tam on the way back.
Chilled photo run (Route 323) — start at Meena Cafe in the rice fields, then move on into Sai Yok for a main meal by the river.
Coming as a group — jungle-style places like Krua Khao Din or Renu work out better for sharing, since the dishes come big.
On a budget — riverside som tam and grilled chicken like Phi Jo or Pak Ban will fill you up for around a hundred baht.

blocks.html: Neither route is that far measured from town, but they head in opposite directions — pick your stops based on the falls you're set on, and you'll make the most of your time. No need to force a stop at every place in one day; save some for next time.

faq.q: Do Erawan Falls and Sai Yok use the same road?
faq.a: No, they're different routes. Erawan and Srinakarin Dam are toward Si Sawat district via Highway 3199, while Sai Yok and Sai Yok Noi Falls are via Highway 323 heading west. They split the moment you leave Kanchanaburi town.

faq.q: Do the restaurants along the way have parking?
faq.a: Most of the places we picked are right on the road or have their own lots — Krua Khao Din, Meena Cafe, and the riverside som tam spots near the dam are easy to pull into without winding down narrow lanes. A few, like Krua Rim Nam Nong Hoi, do require a short turn into a side lane.

faq.q: Should I eat before or after the falls?
faq.a: We'd eat the heavy meal after the falls — the climb up Erawan's tiers is fairly steep, and it's hard going if you're too full. In the morning just stop for a cafe or a snack, and save the jungle-style food and som tam for the afternoon on the way back.

faq.q: Do places around here take cards or bank transfers?
faq.a: Many riverside and jungle-style places are cash-mainly, and some spots have weak mobile signal, so scan-to-pay may not be reliable. Carry cash and you'll have peace of mind.

faq.q: Can I do both routes in a single day from Kanchanaburi?
faq.a: You can, but it'll be very rushed, since the two routes head opposite ways. We'd suggest one waterfall per day so you have time to swim and eat at a relaxed pace. If you want to do both, staying overnight makes it work much better.
